SELECT s.symbol_id, COUNT(*) AS method_count
FROM code.symbols s
JOIN code.class_bases cb ON s.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id
WHERE s.kind = 'class'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM code.files f WHERE f.file_id = s.file_id AND f.is_test = TRUE)
  AND s.qualname NOT LIKE '%.%'
GROUP BY s.symbol_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY method_count DESC, s.symbol_id ASC;

request:
Which classes in the non-test code define at least 20 methods directly in their own body? Count every method definition separately (a property getter and its setter count as two; inherited methods and methods of nested classes do not count). Return each class's symbol ID and its method count, largest count first, ties broken by symbol ID alphabetically.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), method_count (integer). Order the rows as the question asks.
explanation: The query filters symbols to only class kind in non-test files, excludes inherited/nested methods by requiring qualname has no dots, counts each method definition row from class_bases (where ordinal indicates direct definition order), and returns counts sorted descending with alphabetical symbol_id tie-breaking.
sql:
SELECT s.symbol_id, COUNT(*) AS method_count
FROM code.symbols s
JOIN code.class_bases cb ON s.symbol_id = cb.class_symbol_id
WHERE s.kind = 'class'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM code.files f WHERE f.file_id = s.file_id AND f.is_test = TRUE)
  AND s.qualname NOT LIKE '%.%'
GROUP BY s.symbol_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY method_count DESC, s.symbol_id ASC;
